en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Third Chapter
The Discourse on Non-perception: Is there perception among non-percipient beings? Yes.

Is it not the case that there is existence with perception, a destination with perception, an abode for beings with perception, a cycle of rebirth with perception, a womb of perception, and the acquisition of an individuality with perception?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...

Is it not rather the case that there is existence without perception, a destination without perception, an abode for beings without perception, a cycle of rebirth without perception, a womb without perception, and the acquisition of an individuality without perception?
“Yes.

“If it is the case that the state of non-perception, the destiny of non-perception, the abode of non-percipient beings, the cycle of existence of non-percipient beings, the womb of non-percipient beings, and the acquisition of the individual existence of non-percipient beings exist, then indeed you must not say:
‘Perception exists among non-percipient beings.’”
Is there perception among non-percipient beings? Yes.
Is the five-aggregate existence a destiny, an abode of beings, a cycle of existence, a birth-place, and an acquisition of a personal identity? Yes.
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...Is it not the case that a single-aggregate existence is a destination, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a womb, and the acquisition of an individuality?
Yes, it is.
If a single-aggregate existence, a destination, a station for beings, the round of rebirth, a matrix, and the acquisition of an individuality are [identical], then indeed you should not say:
"Perception exists among non-percipient beings.
Does perception exist among non-percipient beings?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does one perform the function of perception by means of that perception?
You should not say so … [and so on] …

Among human beings, there is perception; and is that state of perception, that destination of perception, that abode of beings consisting of perception, that saṃsāra of perception, that womb of perception, that acquisition of an individual existence consisting of perception?

Yes. Among non-percipient beings, is there perception; and is that state of perception, that destination of perception, that abode of beings, that saṃsāra, that womb, that acquisition of an individual existence? No.

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there perception among human beings, and is that five-aggregate existence, a destination, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a womb, and the acquisition of a personal identity? Yes.
In non-percipient beings, perception exists; and is that [existence] a five-aggregate existence, a destiny, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a womb, and the acquisition of a personal identity?
One should not say so… [as before].
Among humans, perception exists; does one perform the function of perception by means of that perception?
“Yes,” [you say].
“In non-percipient beings there is perception; by means of that perception, one performs what is to be done by perception?
One should not speak thus … [as before] … .

Is there perception among non-percipient beings? And is that state of non-perception, the destination of non-percipient beings, the abode of non-percipient beings, the wandering of non-percipient beings, the womb of non-percipient beings, the acquisition of the individual existence of non-percipient beings?
Yes. Is there perception among human beings? And is that state of non-perception, the destination of non-percipient beings... [and so forth]? No.
Is there the acquisition of a non-percipient state of being? One should not say so… [as before] …In the case of non-percipient beings, does perception exist?
And is that a single-aggregate existence, a destiny, an abode of beings, a cycle of rebirth, a womb, or an acquisition of a state of being?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is there perception among human beings, and is that a single-aggregate existence, a destiny, ...
[and] an acquisition of a personal identity?”
It should not be said so ...
[as before] ... Is there perception among the non-percipient beings, yet they do not perform the function of perception by means of that perception? Yes.
“Among human beings perception exists, yet one does not perform the function of perception by means of that perception”?
One should certainly not say so … [as before] … It should not be said—
“Is there perception among non-percipient beings?”—
Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“There are, monks, gods called ‘non-percipient beings’;
with the arising of perception, those gods pass away from that host.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” [you say].
“In that case, does perception exist among non-percipient beings?
“Does perception exist among non-percipient beings?”
"Is it the case that sometimes there is [existence] and sometimes there is not?

That sometimes beings are percipient, sometimes beings are non-percipient; that sometimes there is the state of being percipient, sometimes the state of being non-percipient; and that sometimes there is five-aggregate existence, sometimes one-aggregate existence?
One should certainly not say this... [and so on].
Is perception present among non-percipient beings at some times and absent at other times?
Yes. At what time is it present, and at what time is it absent?
"At the time of death and at the time of rebirth they exist; at the time of stability they do not exist.
At the time of death and at the time of rebirth they are beings with perception; at the time of stability they are non-percipient beings.
At the time of death and at the time of rebirth there is the state of perception; at the time of stability there is the state of non-perception.
Is there fivefold existence at the time of death and at the time of rebirth, and one-fold existence at the time of maintenance?
One should not say so... [and so on].
The Discussion on Non-percipient Beings is concluded.
